# Extend's libadb source

Imported from https://github.com/MuntashirAkon/libadb-android at tag 3.1.1,
commit c849886ebc6d48e7b46d967e78a6bb65c90c3b74.

## Licence

LibADB Android is offered under `GPL-3.0-or-later OR Apache-2.0` (see `COPYING`). Silicon Extend
uses it under the **Apache License 2.0**. Some files also carry other notices, kept in each file
and in `LICENSES/`:

- BSD-3-Clause: `AdbConnection.java`, `AdbProtocol.java`, `AdbStream.java` (Copyright 2013 Cameron
  Gutman) and `AdbAuthenticationFailedException.java` (Copyright 2020 Sam Palmer).
- MIT: `PRNGFixes.java` (Copyright 2013 Google Inc.).
- `AdbPairingRequiredException.java` has no header upstream; `COPYING` covers it.

The app ships these notices and the full licence texts in its **Open-source licences** screen
(`app/src/main/assets/open_source_licences.txt`, generated by `tools/notices/generate_notices.py`).

## SPAKE2 dependency (LGPL-3.0)

Pairing uses `com.github.MuntashirAkon.spake2-java:spake2-android:2.2.1` from JitPack
(source: https://github.com/MuntashirAkon/spake2-java, tag v2.2.1; its native library is built from
https://github.com/MuntashirAkon/spake2-c). It is LGPL-3.0 and ships a prebuilt `libspake2.so`
for four ABIs. How the licence is met:

- It is used unmodified, and the APK's licence screen carries its notice, the LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0
  texts (and LGPL-2.1 and MIT for portions of spake2-c) and the source location.
- Its native code stays a separate shared library (`lib/<abi>/libspake2.so`) that Android loads
  at run time, and its two Java classes are not obfuscated (the app is not minified), so a
  recipient can replace either with an interface-compatible modified version and re-sign the APK.
- Its artifact checksum is pinned in `gradle/verification-metadata.xml`, because JitPack builds
  from a mutable Git tag.

## Changes made by Silicon Extend

Each changed file says so at its top.

- `AdbConnection.java`, `AdbStream.java`: stream opening waits on an acknowledged state under the
  same monitor the connection reader uses, so a loopback peer's answer can't be lost before the
  opener waits; concurrent opens allocate distinct IDs; a cancelled open closes its stream, and when
  the daemon's acknowledgement arrives after the opener gave up, the connection closes the
  daemon's end by its ID (it would otherwise stay open until the connection closes).
- `AdbConnection.java`, `AbsAdbConnectionManager.java`: a connection can require TLS; then a peer
  that answers CNXN in plain text or asks for RSA authentication is refused and never gets a
  signature. Connection failures keep their cause in the message.
- `AbsAdbConnectionManager.java`: `isConnected()` no longer waits for the lock that `connect()`
  and `pair()` hold for their whole timeout; it keeps the GUID the device announced while pairing.
- `PairingConnectionCtx.java`: keeps that GUID (Wireless debugging advertises `adb-<guid>`).
- `AdbProtocol.java`: OPEN destinations are sized by their UTF-8 bytes; commands containing
  non-ASCII text failed with `BufferOverflowException`.
- `AdbConnection.java`, `AdbStream.java`: flow control. Upstream answered every WRTE with OKAY as
  soon as it arrived and queued the payload without bound, so a fast command (`head -c 270000000
  /dev/zero`) or a large pull filled the heap and crashed the app with `OutOfMemoryError`. Now the
  OKAY is sent when the stream's reader takes the payload (outside the queue's lock), so the daemon,
  which sends one WRTE per OKAY, pauses until the app has read. A peer that sends more than eight
  unacknowledged payloads on one stream loses that stream (CLSE, and the reader gets the reason via
  `AdbStream.getFailure()`).

`src/test/.../ExtendTransportTest.java` covers these changes against a scripted peer. The Android
instrumentation suite exercises real loopback shell, file transfer, installation, cancellation, TLS
pairing and discovery. Keep transport changes here, at their owning code.
